items.title: Ron Carter interviewed by Monk Rowe, New York City, New York, January 17, 1999
items.q: Maynard Ferguson Big Band with Wayne Shorter and Slide Hampton

ctx.x: How did your professors feel about that? Or wasn’t it even an issue for them?

Well most of them didn’t really care. I went to class on time and did the homework. Some of them didn’t care for that kind of music so they didn’t like what I did in classes, and the school did not encourage a jazz profile. And the strange thing is at that time there was the Eastman Theater, there was a show called “Jazz for Moderns” that would travel throughout the country. And they played at the Eastman Theater, it was a wonderful auditorium, it seated maybe 2,000 people. And they had great bands going all…
force in music, it’s hard to understand how a classical institution would continue to ignore its presence.

items.title: Wayne Shorter — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History
items.q: Ron Carter already did something... Outside, before the semester started. You heard about the Monk Institute will be housed at UCLA now.

ctx.x: Yeah. “Don’t be... You’re eating in a French restaurant or the hotel or whatever, and keep bragging about how great the subway [sic] sandwich... And about how they treat people. He was talking to someone thick-headed. He said, “you’re still on the bandstand when you’re walking down the street, and when you’re playing...” We played a lot of club concerts then, too. “When you’re playing in a club, don’t be arrogant to the waiters and everything; we’ve got to come back here maybe 15 years from now, and that waiter…

There’s something I didn’t know about Art Blakey. When I was doing...asked to do certain (over the years) interviews, I caught myself going back about Miles a lot, and Weather Report...Miles... But kind of recently, I caught myself. Wait a minute. I had five years with Art Blakey, and in those interviews I didn’t talk about it. But there was something about Art... Ok. I practice Buddhism. I’ll just leave it right there. But Herbie and I are...there’s a dialogue that we have had with a president of this Buddhist…
